instruction: Look at freecad_task-8_input.step in FreeCAD. Use the Part Design workbench throughout; activate the Body, create new sketches on the required faces or planes, and complete all fused features in the same Body using GUI additive and subtractive features. Convert the lug blank into a clevis bracket with mounting details. Keep the base plate fixed. Cut a central fork gap through the upright lug: the gap is 24 mm wide along X, extends through the lug along Y, starts at Z=31 mm, and continues to the top, leaving two separate upper ears still joined by the base. Cut a coaxial pin hole of diameter 16 mm through both ears along the Y direction, centered at (60,35,50). Add two triangular side ribs, each exactly 5 mm thick along Y: the front rib spans Y=18 to 23 mm and has XZ triangle vertices (33,14), (48,14), and (48,44); the rear rib spans Y=47 to 52 mm and has XZ triangle vertices (72,14), (87,14), and (72,44). Cut four base mounting holes of diameter 7 mm at (24,18), (96,18), (24,52), and (96,52), each with a top counterbore of diameter 14 mm and depth 5 mm. Export /home/user/Desktop/freecad_task-8_output.step using the GUI only; no external scripts.
